model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25 year) total revenues, US$m, from EXR_Metrics.csv / 10-K FY2025 (property rental + tenant reinsurance + management fees and other income). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow that is valued is Core FFO (EXR's own non-GAAP measure: NAREIT FFO plus the non-cash amortisation of the Life Storage debt discount and of merger-related intangibles) less an assumed recurring-capex charge, i.e. AFFO. Core FFO / revenue was 53.9% in FY2025 (1,820.8 / 3,377.5), 55.3% in FY2024 (1,799.6 / 3,256.9), 53.6% in H1-2026 (926.6 / 1,730.2) and 54.1% in H1-2025. Note Core FFO includes ~US$163m (FY2025) of interest income on the bridge-loan book and ~US$69m of equity in earnings of unconsolidated JVs, which sit BELOW revenue in the income statement; the margin therefore runs above the property-level NOI margin net of interest and G&A.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted on the FFO-per-share basis: 210.96m weighted basic common shares (Q2 2026 10-Q) + 9.40m common OP units assumed redeemed for common + unvested awards = 221.00m weighted diluted shares used for Q2 2026 Core FFO per share (Q2 2026 release: 221,002,914) and the FY2026 guidance share count (221.0m, 'assumes redemption of all OP units for common stock'). Basic shares on issue were 211,273,076 at 30-Jun-2026 and 211,269,558 at 24-Jul-2026. Held FLAT: the buyback is opportunistic (US$149.5m in FY2025 at ~US$129.80 avg, US$1.4m in H1-2026, US$349.0m authorisation remaining) and roughly offsets restricted-stock issuance; no ATM issuance in 2026 (US$800m capacity unused); SBC (US$35.5m FY2025) is expensed inside G&A and therefore inside Core FFO, so charging further dilution would double count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is Core FFO less recurring capex, which is already AFTER interest expense (FY2025 interest expense US$587.6m cash-basis plus US$47.5m non-cash discount amortisation; FY2026 guidance US$595-598m cash interest). Deducting the balance-sheet net debt on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit and leverage context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m carrying value at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet): secured notes payable, net 1,073.3 + unsecured term loans, net 1,495.4 + unsecured senior notes, net 9,460.9 (face 9,675.0 less 164.2 Life Storage fair-value discount) + revolving lines of credit and commercial paper 1,617.0 (of which commercial paper 850.0) = 13,646.6. Face value 13,867.9. Excludes operating lease liabilities of 767.6. 78.5% fixed-rate (88.4% effective net of variable-rate bridge-loan receivables), combined weighted average rate 4.3%, weighted average maturity ~4.0 years. Post balance date: US$600m of senior notes repaid at maturity on 1-Jul-2026 (pre-funded, hence the elevated cash) and US$550m 4.90% senior notes due Feb-2032 issued 6-Jul-2026.
inputs.cash_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q). Elevated versus the ~US$110-140m run-rate because it pre-funded the US$600m 1-Jul-2026 note maturity; pro forma for that repayment cash is ~US$95m. Not used in the valuation (net_debt held at zero).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO proxy, US$m: Core FFO 1,820.845 less assumed recurring capital expenditure of 3.0% of revenue (101.3; see capex_rationale in each scenario) = 1,719.5, i.e. US$7.75 per FFO-basis share against a US$6.48 dividend (84% AFFO payout, 79% Core FFO payout). EXR does not publish AFFO or recurring capex, so this bridge is an analyst assumption, flagged as such. NOT the CSV free_cash_flow of 1,288.5 (OCF 1,850.2 less 561.7 of 'PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets', which bundles acquisitions and development), and NOT reported FFO of 1,752.8.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Core FFO attributable to common stockholders and unit holders, US$m (Q4 2025 earnings release 19-Feb-2026), US$8.21 per diluted share on 221.89m shares, +1.1% on FY2024's 1,799.6 / US$8.12. NAREIT FFO FY2025 was 1,752.8 / US$7.90; the 68.0 difference is non-cash amortisation of the Life Storage debt discount (47.5) and merger intangibles net of tax (~16) plus small other items. GAAP net income (974.0 attributable to common) is after 715.2 of real-estate depreciation and is not used anywhere in this valuation.
inputs.sbc_note: Zero in the flow because share-based compensation (US$35.5m FY2025; US$16.4m H1-2026, 10-Q cash flow statement 'Compensation expense related to share-based awards') is a G&A expense inside net income and is NOT added back in FFO or Core FFO. It is therefore already charged. Share count held flat for the same reason.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 consolidated statement of cash flows, 'Compensation expense related to share-based awards' US$35,537 thousand; Q2 2026 10-Q same line US$16,443 thousand for H1-2026. Expensed inside Core FFO; not deducted a second time.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero deduction. EXR's US$163.2m (FY2025; FY2026 guidance US$153-154m) of interest income is earned on a ~US$1.5bn bridge-loan book to storage operators and on OP-unit-holder notes -- it is an operating lending business that also feeds the acquisition pipeline, not a yield on surplus cash, and EXR carries no net cash. It stays in the flow.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases US$149.5m (Q4 2025 mostly, avg ~US$129.80/share); H1-2026 US$1.4m; US$349.0m authorisation remaining at 30-Jun-2026. Treated as opportunistic, not a driver: share count held flat.
inputs.dividend_note: US$1.62 per quarter, unchanged since Q3 2023; FY2025 common dividends paid US$1,374.3m plus ~US$61m of OP-unit distributions. Payout 79% of Core FFO, ~84% of the AFFO proxy; the dividend is covered but leaves only ~US$290m/yr of retained AFFO for the ~US$300m/yr acquisition programme, so external growth is largely debt- and JV-funded within the current leverage.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation written before Monday 2026-09-28 open)
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury ~4.2% + equity risk premium 5.0% x REIT beta ~0.85 = ~8.5% base. Cross-checks: the stock trades at 16.0x FY2026E Core FFO (6.2% FFO yield) and ~17x the AFFO proxy, and a 4.9% dividend yield growing ~2-4%, i.e. the market itself is pricing a ~7.5-9% equity return. Bear 9.5% (higher-for-longer rates: EXR is the most rate-sensitive name in the storage group by dividend yield and leverage), bull 8.0%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease liabilities (US$767.6m, ground leases) stay OUT of debt and their rent stays inside property operating expense, i.e. inside Core FFO. Charged once, in the flow.
inputs.nci_treatment: Common OP units (9.40m) are included in the 221.0m share count and their share of Core FFO is included in the numerator (Core FFO is 'attributable to common stockholders and unit holders'), so they are treated as equity. Preferred OP units (US$47.8m carrying value at 30-Jun-2026) are not convertible into the share count on the FFO basis; their distributions are inside the FFO add-back for NCI, so they are deducted at carrying value in equity_bridge (~US$0.22/share). Other consolidated JV NCI is immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine (same pattern as BXP, GPT.AX, GMG.AX, CHC.AX). Why: Extra Space is a self-storage REIT whose GAAP net income is after US$715m/yr of real-estate depreciation on assets that appreciate, so P/E, NetMargin and the CSV FreeCashFlow (which nets acquisition and development spend) are meaningless; the flow the equity actually receives is Core FFO less recurring capex, which is already after interest. Engine mapping: growth_rates drive total revenue; ebitda_margin_path is READ AS Core FFO / revenue (post-interest, post-G&A, post-TRS tax); capex_pct_path is the recurring-capex FFO-to-AFFO bridge; sbc, D&A, lease and cash-tax paths are all zero because those items are already inside Core FFO; wacc is the cost of equity; net_debt is zero; terminal_cap_multiple caps the exit at 15-18x AFFO. Fresh build (no prior DCF, no MEMORY.md entry). FY0 = FY2025; Y1 = FY2026, of which three quarters have elapsed at the valuation date -- discounting Y1 a full year is slightly conservative. House and street bases coincide (no SBC add-back in the flow), so band_position is null by construction. Ticker straddles no other model row: the third-party management (1,964 stores), bridge lending (~US$1.5bn) and tenant reinsurance businesses are all inside Core FFO and are valued with it, not separately.
inputs.data_vintage: Price: Yahoo Finance chart API at price_as_of. Balance sheet, share count, interest, dividends: Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-31) and Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K 2026-07-28). Core FFO history: Q4 2025 release (8-K 2026-02-19), Q4 2023 release (8-K 2024-02-27), Q4 2021 release (8-K 2022-02-23). Revenue/GAAP history: EXR_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL).

equity_bridge.item: Preferred Operating Partnership units at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, 30-Jun-2026; not in the 221.0m FFO-basis share count, distributions inside the FFO NCI add-back, so deducted here once.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: Core FFO PER SHARE (the owner flow on the per-share basis the valuation uses): FY2022 ~US$8.44 (derived: FY2023's US$8.10 was reported as a 4.0% decrease) -> FY2025 US$8.21 = -0.9% p.a. over 3 years; FY2021 US$6.91 -> FY2025 US$8.21 = +4.4% p.a. over FOUR years (the '5yr' field carries the 4-year figure because the FY2020 release was not fetched). Dollar Core FFO grew far faster (FY2021 974.0 -> FY2025 1,820.8, +17% p.a.) because the Life Storage merger (Jul-2023) issued ~78m shares.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Average of the base-case revenue path (FY2026 guidance year plus a supply-driven recovery fading to 2.5%); historical CAGRs are unusable as a forward anchor because every series is distorted by the all-stock Life Storage merger.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (+20.6%/+20.0%), equity (+52%/+37%) and EPS (-10.5%/+4.3%) CAGRs diverge by far more than 30% because the Jul-2023 Life Storage merger roughly doubled revenue and equity and diluted per-share earnings; none of them describes organic growth. Same-store revenue growth was +3.1% (FY2023), ~-0.5% (FY2024), +0.1% (FY2025) and +2.0% (H1-2026). Core FFO per share has been flat for three years (8.44 -> 8.10 -> 8.12 -> 8.21) while interest expense rose from ~US$300m pre-merger to US$588m.
historical_growth.notes: Equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor: book equity of a REIT is depreciated historical cost and moved by merger accounting, not by retained earnings. Reported FCF CAGR is not computed: the CSV capex line bundles acquisitions and development.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 (Y1) 3.7%: H1-2026 revenue was +4.1% YoY on the 2025 acquisition cohort (76 wholly-owned stores, US$926m) and +2.0% same-store; guidance for FY same-store revenue of 1-2% implies H2 deceleration to ~1%, with US$300m of 2026 acquisitions and the C of O pipeline adding ~1.5-2%. FY2027-FY2029 3.8-4.0%: industry deliveries fall to ~2.4% of stock in 2026 versus a ~4.2% long-run average, 16 of the top 20 markets already show positive move-in rate growth, and existing-customer rate increases compound; plus ~1% p.a. external growth from acquisitions/JVs and the third-party platform (1,964 managed stores, +108 net in H1-2026) feeding the roll-up pipeline. Fades to 3.0-3.5% mid-decade as the supply tailwind normalises, and to 2.5% (CPI-like rent growth, no cap-rate expansion) by FY2034.
base.margin_rationale: READ AS Core FFO / total revenue (post-interest). Y1 52.8% on 3.7% revenue growth gives FY2026E Core FFO of ~US$1,849m = US$8.37 per share on the guided 221.0m count -- the upper half of the twice-raised US$8.25-8.40 range, consistent with H1 at +3.5% and Q2 at +4.9% but honouring the guided H2 deceleration (tougher comps, the 1-Jul refinancing of US$600m at a higher coupon, US$0.17 of C of O dilution). Dips to 52.7% in FY2027 as ~US$3.5bn/yr of debt keeps repricing from Life-Storage-era coupons toward ~4.9-5.2% (interest expense +6.6% in FY2025, +1.9% in H1-2026, against ~3% NOI growth), then recovers ~0.1-0.2pt/yr from FY2028 as same-store NOI growth (79% NOI margin, fixed G&A of ~US$189m) outruns interest cost. Capped at 53.5%, below the FY2024 55.3% peak, because the 2024 margin embedded a lower interest bill than the refinanced book will carry.
base.capex_rationale: Recurring (maintenance) capital expenditure as the FFO-to-AFFO bridge, at 3.0% of total revenue = ~US$101m in FY2025 terms. EXR does NOT disclose recurring capex or AFFO; the 10-K cash flow shows 'Purchase of equipment and fixtures' of US$21.1m (FY2025) / US$20.5m (FY2024) and 'Development and redevelopment' of US$143.0m / US$128.6m, the latter mostly C of O and expansion projects that generate the growth in the revenue path. 3.0% of revenue is ~US$0.65 per REIT-owned square foot, between CubeSmart's disclosed recurring capex (~US$0.30-0.40/sq ft) and Public Storage's 'capital to maintain real estate' (~US$0.80-0.95/sq ft including its Property-of-Tomorrow programme), and roughly 3.7% of property rental revenue once the capex-free tenant-reinsurance and management-fee streams (~14% of revenue) are excluded. Growth capex (US$300m/yr acquisitions, development) is funded from retained AFFO (~US$290m/yr) plus debt at constant leverage and is what the growth path pays for; it is not deducted again.
base.tax_rationale: Zero because Core FFO is already after the taxable-REIT-subsidiary income tax on the tenant-reinsurance and management businesses (FY2026 guidance US$48-49m; FY2025 cash taxes US$35.3m); the REIT itself distributes >90% of taxable income and pays no entity-level tax.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5% / 2.5% = 17.1x terminal AFFO (5.9% AFFO yield, ~16x Core FFO) binds below the 18x cap. Storage REITs have traded at 15-25x FFO over the last decade; 17x on a 10-year-out flow assumes no multiple expansion from today's 16x.

bull.growth_rationale: Supply trough is deeper and longer than guided (deliveries stay ~2% of stock through 2028 as construction financing remains scarce), housing turnover recovers as mortgage rates ease, and same-store revenue runs +3.5-4.5% in FY2027-FY2029 on occupancy back above 94.5% plus double-digit new-customer rate gains; the bridge-loan book (US$1.5bn) and 2,373 managed/JV stores convert into US$500m+/yr of acquisitions at 6%+ going-in yields funded by cheaper debt. Fades to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Core FFO / revenue reaches the FY2024 55.3% level by FY2030 as revenue growth on a ~79% NOI-margin base outruns a stable-to-falling interest bill (rates ease, 88% effectively fixed) and G&A stays flat in dollars; tenant reinsurance (US$294-296m net income guided for 2026) and management fees grow faster than property revenue. Y1 53.2% = FY2026E Core FFO US$8.50, a Q3/Q4 beat-and-raise above the current US$8.40 high end.
bull.capex_rationale: Recurring capex at 2.5% of revenue (~US$0.55/sq ft), the low end of the peer range, on a young post-Life-Storage-refresh portfolio.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0% / 3.0% = 20.6x would exceed the 18x AFFO cap, so the cap binds: even the bull case does not pay more than 18x for the year-10 flow.

bear.growth_rationale: Recovery stalls: a weaker housing/labour market cuts move-ins, Public Storage (now ~14% share post-NSA) and CubeSmart compete on promotional rates in the oversupplied Sunbelt, and same-store revenue is flat-to-+1% in FY2027-FY2028 with occupancy drifting toward 93%; acquisitions slow to ~US$150m/yr because retained AFFO is thin and the equity is too expensive to issue. Y1 3.0% keeps FY2026 at the low end of guidance. Long-run 2% = inflation minus attrition.
bear.margin_rationale: Core FFO / revenue compresses ~3pts by FY2029 as US$13.9bn of debt reprices at 5.0-5.5% in a higher-for-longer rate environment (+US$100m/yr of interest = ~3% of revenue) while property taxes, insurance and marketing outgrow flat rents; Y1 52.5% = FY2026E Core FFO US$8.26, the guidance low end. Held flat thereafter -- no further compression, no recovery.
bear.capex_rationale: Recurring capex at 3.5% of revenue (~US$0.75/sq ft), toward Public Storage's disclosed level, as the older Life Storage assets need roofing, paving and HVAC catch-up and the company invests defensively in solar/LED and technology.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.0% = 13.6x terminal AFFO binds below the 15x cap -- a de-rating to the low end of the sector's historical range in a structurally higher-rate world.

scenario_narratives.base: Self-storage's 2023-2025 rate reset is over and the sector grinds higher on falling new supply: same-store revenue +2-3.5% through FY2029, external growth of ~1%/yr from the acquisition pipeline that the management and bridge-lending platforms feed, and a Core FFO margin held near 53% as debt repricing is roughly offset by operating leverage. Core FFO per share moves from US$8.21 (FY2025) to ~US$8.37 (FY2026, upper half of guidance) and compounds ~3.5% a year thereafter; the US$6.48 dividend is ~84% covered by AFFO and grows once the payout normalises. Capitalised at an 8.5% cost of equity with 2.5% terminal growth (17x AFFO exit).
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply drought (deliveries ~2% of stock for several years), a housing-turnover recovery as mortgage rates ease, and a lower interest bill produce +4.5-5% revenue growth in FY2027-FY2029 with the Core FFO margin back at the FY2024 peak of ~55%. Scale (4,300+ stores, the largest data set in the sector) lets EXR out-price peers and buy US$500m+/yr of stores from refinancing-stressed private owners. Discounted at 8.0% with the exit capped at 18x AFFO.
scenario_narratives.bear: Higher-for-longer rates reprice US$13.9bn of debt at 5%+, a soft housing and labour market keeps move-ins weak, and PSA/NSA and CubeSmart compete on rate in oversupplied Sunbelt markets, so same-store revenue is flat and the Core FFO margin compresses ~3pts to ~50.5%. Core FFO per share is stuck near US$8 for years, the dividend is only just covered by AFFO, and the shares de-rate to ~13-14x AFFO at a 9.5% cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the growth-company 15/50/35 default. Bear kept at 25% because the valuation is dominated by the discount rate and EXR is the most rate-sensitive of the storage REITs (4.9% dividend yield, ~6x net debt/EBITDA, four-year weighted debt maturity), and because three years of flat Core FFO per share show the recovery is not yet in the numbers. Bull kept to 25% because storage is a commodity product with low switching costs and the PSA-NSA combination removes EXR's scale lead; the bull case needs both a supply trough and lower rates.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Extra Space is valued on the cash the equity actually receives: Core FFO less an assumed recurring-capex charge (AFFO), capitalised at a cost of equity, with no separate deduction for the US$13.6bn of debt because the flow is already after US$590m+/yr of interest. GAAP earnings, book value and the CSV free-cash-flow line are all ignored as measures of value -- the first two because real-estate depreciation and merger accounting make them meaningless, the last because it nets acquisitions and development. The three scenarios differ mainly on where same-store revenue growth settles as new supply falls, how much of the operating recovery the refinancing of Life-Storage-era debt absorbs, and the cost of equity; the terminal exit is capped at 15-18x AFFO so that no scenario relies on the sector re-rating above where it trades today (16x FFO). At the Friday close the shares sit close to the probability-weighted value: a fairly-priced, high-quality compounder yielding 4.9% rather than a bargain.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate risk dominates: each 100bp on the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 15-20%; a 10-year Treasury sustainably above 5% pushes the stock toward the bear value.
Refinancing drag: ~US$3.5bn/yr of debt reprices at 4.9-5.5% against Life-Storage-era coupons; the margin path assumes operating leverage offsets it and the bear case assumes it does not.

The recurring-capex bridge (3.0% of revenue) is an analyst assumption because EXR does not disclose AFFO or maintenance capex; each 1pt of revenue is ~US$0.15/share of AFFO and ~US$2.50-3.00/share of value.

Supply and competition: the base case leans on industry deliveries falling to ~2.4% of stock; a renewed development wave in the Sunbelt or aggressive promotional pricing by the enlarged Public Storage would push same-store revenue back to flat.
Demand cyclicality: move-ins track housing turnover and small-business formation; a recession would hit occupancy (94.2% at Jun-26) and new-customer rates simultaneously.

Bridge-loan book (~US$1.5bn, ~US$150m/yr of interest income inside Core FFO) carries credit risk to private storage operators; a default cycle would cut Core FFO and force consolidation of impaired collateral.
Leadership transition: new CFO (Jan-2026) and new CEO (Jan-2027) during the post-merger integration period.
Regulatory: state/municipal rent-regulation or tenant-notice rules for storage, and state insurance oversight of the tenant-reinsurance subsidiary (US$294-296m net income guided for 2026).
